candidates.issueBody:
### Reproduction link

[![Edit on CodeSandbox](https://codesandbox.io/static/img/play-codesandbox.svg)](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/pedantic-scooby-mn9kjr)

### Steps to reproduce

Open select and navigate down with keyboard

### What is expected?

When using the Select in a way which means that results are paginated (using `onPopupScroll` to load more results) the additional request would typically happens when the user has navigated to the last option or close-to-last option. After fetching new results, the position the user was at should persist and they should be able to continue navigating through the options.

### What is actually happening?

The selected option is always reset to the first whenever the menu length changes, meaning whereever the user was in the options was not saved, making it inconvenient to traverse the select with a keyboard

| Environment | Info |
| --- | --- |
| antd | 6.3.5 |
| React | 18.3.1 |
| System | Mac Os 15.6.1 |
| Browser | Chromium 146.0.7680.178 |

---
This was also reported here: https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/12440#issuecomment-1761351991

Root cause: https://github.com/react-component/select/blob/740b93b18ac16060f5bdadee63555a2dcffb094f/src/OptionList.tsx#L136

Suggestion: Only run this useEffect on searchValue change, or provide a prop to disable the setting.

Ps: Maybe also worth mentioning that `defaultActiveFirstOption` isn't actually used as expected, since it only gets considered in the useEffect, not when the component first mounts.

<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @roztyree-eero! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the ant-design team.

<!-- Answer -->
This is a valid accessibility concern. The Tag close icon currently renders as a `<span>` element [[1]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/dce9f138cb06cc679f889f5d20c0a0c3e5a7d268/components/tag/index.tsx#L183-L186), which means it's not in the tab order and has no semantic button role — exactly as you described.

Notably, **other Ant Design components already handle this correctly**. For example, the Alert component's close icon uses a `<button type="button">` with `tabIndex={0}` and proper ARIA attributes [[2]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/dce9f138cb06cc679f889f5d20c0a0c3e5a7d268/components/alert/Alert.tsx#L140-L156). Both Tag and Alert share the same `useClosable` hook [[3]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/dce9f138cb06cc679f889f5d20c0a0c3e5a7d268/components/_util/hooks/useClosable.tsx#L165-L182) for ARIA label management, but Tag doesn't render the close icon as a focusable, semantic element like Alert does.

The recent [PR #57331](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/57331) added semantic styling support (`classNames.close` / `styles.close`) for the Tag close icon, but it didn't change the underlying `<span>` to a `<button>`.

To fix this, the Tag component's close icon should follow the same pattern as Alert:

1. Render as `<button type="button">` instead of `<span>`
2. Include `tabIndex={0}` for keyboard focusability
3. The `aria-label` is already provided via `useClosable` — just needs to be passed through to the button

This would be a relatively contained change in the Tag component's rendering logic, aligning it with the accessibility patterns already established across Alert, Modal, and Notification.

Hi @CodePangZ! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I'm helping the Ant Design team.

`form.getFieldInstance(name)` 返回的其实是通过 React ref 机制捕获到的**组件实例**（即组件通过 `React.forwardRef` + `useImperativeHandle` 暴露出来的内容）[[1]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/d6a2656a8ef1a89d89f49486f2062b0304725f22/components/form/hooks/useForm.ts#L86-L89)。你看到的 `{focus, blur, scrollTo}` 并不是固定返回这些，而是取决于对应表单控件（如 Input、Select 等）在 ref 上暴露了哪些方法。大多数 antd 表单组件约定暴露 `focus` 和 `blur` 用于编程式控制 [[2]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/d6a2656a8ef1a89d89f49486f2062b0304725f22/components/form/hooks/useForm.ts#L78-L84)。

**关于为什么不返回 props：** 这是设计上的考虑——`getFieldInstance` 的定位是提供**命令式控制**（聚焦、失焦等），而非获取组件的配置或属性。表单的状态管理和展示层是解耦的。如果你需要获取字段相关的数据，可以使用其他 Form API：

- `form.getFieldValue(name)` — 获取字段值
- `form.getFieldsValue()` — 获取多个/全部字段值
- `form.getFieldError(name)` — 获取字段校验错误
- `form.isFieldTouched(name)` — 字段是否被操作过

目前没有公开 API 可以直接获取 FormItem 或其子组件的 props。你具体想通过 `getFieldInstance` 获取哪些 props 信息呢？了解具体场景的话，也许可以推荐更合适的方案。

`getFieldInstance` 返回的是组件通过 ref 暴露的实例，Select 的 ref 只暴露了 `focus()` 和 `blur()` 两个方法 [[1]](https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/blob/d6a2656a8ef1a89d89f49486f2062b0304725f22/components/select/index.en-US.md#L143-L148)，不包含 `options` 等 props 信息。这是 React ref 机制的设计限制——ref 用于暴露命令式方法，而非组件的 props。

Form API 的设计目标是管理字段的**值**（value），而不是组件的 **props**。要获取 Select 的 options，建议将 options 放在组件状态中单独管理：

```tsx
const [options, setOptions] = useState([
  { label: 'Option A', value: 'a' },
  { label: 'Option B', value: 'b' },
]);

<Form.Item name="selectField">
  <Select options={options} />
</Form.Item>

// 需要时直接从 state 读取 options
console.log(options);
```

如果你需要获取的是已选中的值而非 options 列表，可以用 `form.getFieldValue('selectField')` [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/1305af31-9246-4d2d-add3-27e8cdd7f529/documents/f5f9b88c-2516-4e59-906e-3ae77a9da7c8)。

The overview search input uses `variant="borderless"` and should keep the current no-border visual style when focused on this page.

This was introduced by https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/pull/58250 / commit `e9bdc2c103c14942dbf5d45f5c82139542fedca6` on 2026-06-15.

That PR added `:focus-visible` outline styles for borderless input-like components:

```ts
const borderlessFocusVisibleSelector =
  '&:focus-visible, &:has(input:focus-visible), &:has(textarea:focus-visible)';
```

The Components Overview page search input is implemented in `.dumi/theme/builtins/ComponentOverview/index.tsx` with:

```tsx
<Input
  autoFocus
  variant="borderless"
  suffix={<SearchOutlined />}
/>
```

So the new borderless focus outline is now visible on the overview page search input.

candidates.title: Focus trap incorrectly finds tabbable elements
candidates.reason: Not admitted: working stable pair, applicable fix and original keyboard task not yet jointly established.
candidates.issueBody:
### Summary:
The regex to determine focusable elements is not specific enough.

https://github.com/reactjs/react-modal/blob/v3.16.1/src/helpers/tabbable.js#L16
```
const tabbableNode = /input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/;
```

In the world of web-components, it is very common to have these names be used in the element tag. Say I have an internal library or a library pulled from the community that is solely build with web-components. Unlike react, the web-component name shows as part of the DOM Tree.
```
<awesome-button>
  <button ...></button>
</awesome-button>

<awesome-input-field>
  <input ... />
</awesome-input-field>
```

The regex is matching both `<awesome-button>` and `<button>` as focusable. With this, the `head` and `tail` checks don't work correctly.
https://github.com/reactjs/react-modal/blob/v3.16.1/src/helpers/scopeTab.js#L32-L38

### Steps to reproduce:

Created a codepen https://codepen.io/bouncehead13/pen/WNabvGY where focus does not stay trap.

The general problem is all with the regex matcher being too broad with its checks.
 1. `/input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/.test('button')` -- GOOD
 2. `/input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/.test('awesome-button')` -- Should not match, but does
 3. `/input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/.test('input')` -- GOOD
 4. `/input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/.test('awesome-input-field')` -- Should not match, but does

### Expected behavior:
Only true focusable nodes are allowed.

### Proposed solution:
Instead of the regex checking as 'contains', change it to enforce 'full word' matches
```
// bad, checks nodeName is anywhere
const tabbableNode = /input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe/;

// good, matches whole nodeName `/^(...)$/`
const tabbableNode = /^(input|select|textarea|button|object|iframe)$/;
```

candidates.title: [Drawer] Content-sized drawer is mispositioned when the virtual keyboard opens on iOS

candidates.issueBody:
## Current behavior

When using `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider`, a content-sized drawer is positioned incorrectly after focusing an input and opening the virtual keyboard on iOS.

The issue is reproducible with a minimal drawer containing a single input.

In Chrome on iOS:

- The drawer moves higher than necessary.
- A large empty area appears between the drawer content and the keyboard.
- Vertical scrolling becomes possible.

In Safari on iOS:

- Extra empty space appears below the drawer content.

The problem reproduces consistently, although its exact visual behavior may vary.

A related issue also occurs in the official **Virtual keyboard aware drawer** example:

https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer#virtual-keyboard-aware

In the official example, the problem reproduces only in Chrome on iOS when focusing an input near the bottom of the drawer. The other inputs behave normally. The official example works correctly in Safari on the same device.

## Reproduction steps

### Content-sized drawer

1. Open the live reproduction on a physical iPhone:
   https://base-ui-drawer-ios-repro.vercel.app/
2. Press **Open keyboard-aware drawer**.
3. Tap the input.
4. Wait for the virtual keyboard to appear.
5. Observe the position and scrollable area of the drawer.

### Official documentation example

1. Open the following page in Chrome on iOS:
   https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer#virtual-keyboard-aware
2. Open the **Virtual keyboard aware drawer** example.
3. Focus an input near the bottom of the drawer.
4. Observe that the drawer content may move outside the visible viewport.
5. In some cases, the layout does not recover until another tap or until the keyboard is closed.

## Expected behavior

A content-sized drawer should retain its content-based height and move only as much as necessary to remain above the virtual keyboard.

Focusing an input should not introduce:

- A large empty area between the drawer content and the keyboard.
- Additional vertical scrolling.
- Extra bottom spacing.
- A temporary or persistent shift outside the visible viewport.

## Reproducible example

- Live reproduction: https://base-ui-drawer-ios-repro.vercel.app/
- Source code: https://github.com/k4dykovv/base-ui-drawer-ios-repro
- Related documentation example: https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer#virtual-keyboard-aware

The reproduction is based on the official example, with all but one input removed and no footer. The original styles and the unmodified `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider` are used. The drawer has `height: auto` and sizes itself to its content.

## Base UI version

```text
1.8.0
```

## Browser and OS

```text
Device: Physical iPhone
OS: iOS 26.4
Chrome: 153.0.8010.24 (Official Build), stable
Safari: iOS 26.4
```

## Additional context

Videos are attached showing:

1. The content-sized drawer with one input in Chrome on iOS.
2. The content-sized drawer with one input in Safari on iOS.
3. The official documentation example in Chrome on iOS.

As a diagnostic experiment, I used a local workaround that synchronizes the viewport container’s position and height with `window.visualViewport` in response to viewport changes. This completely removes the issue in the minimal reproduction.

Videos demonstrating the issue:

### Safari on iOS — content-sized drawer with a single input

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feee4601-3cab-49c3-a652-7ebedee778ec

### Chrome on iOS — content-sized drawer with a single input

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f316270-bf31-4be3-9bfa-b827602019fc

### Chrome on iOS — official Virtual keyboard aware drawer example

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c397ebb-0b1e-4f3b-8b7b-d3f788c9ee17

candidates.title: [popover] Tabbing out of a non-modal popup with no focusable content and no other tabbable page element throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
candidates.reason: Fix5733 identified; useTriggerFocusGuards is byte-identical in published1.6.0/1.7.0, so cannot claim that pair is a regression.
candidates.issueBody:
## Current behavior When a non-modal `Popover.Popup` (the default; `modal={false}`) contains no focusable descendants, and the page has no other tabbable element besides the trigger itself, pressing Tab once while focus is inside the popup crashes the page with: ``` RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded ``` The crash comes from infinite mutual recursion between the trigger's two focus-guard handlers in `useTriggerFocusGuards`: - `handleFocusTargetFocus` (`packages/react/src/utils/popups/useTriggerFocusGuards.ts#L62-L92`) closes the popup and looks for the next tabbable element with: ```ts let nextTabbable = getTabbableAfterElement( store.context.triggerFocusTargetRef.current || triggerElementRef.current, ); ``` - `getTabbableAfterElement` → `getTabbableNearElement` (`packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/utils/tabbable.ts#L226-L244`) builds the full tabbable list for `document.body` and picks the next entry **modulo the list length**: ```ts const nextIndex = (index + dir + elementCount) % elementCount; return list[nextIndex]; ``` - `FocusGuard` elements are themselves tabbable (`tabIndex: 0`, `packages/react/src/utils/FocusGuard.tsx#L26-L30`), so once the popup is closed and its own two "inside" guards have unmounted, the only tabbable elements left in `document.body` are the trigger's own guards and the trigger button — three elements total. Asking for "the tabbable element after the last one" wraps around to the *first* one instead of returning nothing, so the trigger's after-guard resolves to the trigger's **own pre-guard**. - Focusing the pre-guard runs `handlePreFocusGuardFocus` (`useTriggerFocusGuards.ts#L44-L60`), which does the mirror-image lookup with `getTabbableBeforeElement` — which wraps around the same three-element list back to the after-guard, and focuses it. - Each of these `.focus()` calls synchronously re-enters the other handler (DOM focus event handlers run synchronously inside `.focus()`), so the two handlers call each other with no termination condition, growing the native call stack until it overflows. Both handlers already know they can be called again on the *same* trigger — `handleFocusTargetFocus` guards its own `while` loop that walks forward from `getTabbableAfterElement` with `getNextTabbable` (which is index-clamped, not modulo) and a `break` when the same element repeats — but that loop only starts *after* the modulo wraparound has already produced the wrong first `nextTabbable`, so the guard never gets a chance to run: the recursion actually happens across handlers, one call each, not inside the loop. ## Expected behavior Tabbing out of an empty non-modal popup on a page with no other tabbable elements should close the popup and move focus somewhere sane (document body, or simply stay on/after the trigger) without throwing. `getTabbableAfterElement`/`getTabbableBeforeElement` returning a *different trigger's own guard* as "the next tabbable element" looks like the root cause — a bounded, non-modular list walk (matching what `getNextTabbable`/`getPreviousTabbable` already do) would stop this handoff from looping back into the same trigger's guards. ## Reproducible example No dependency on any app code — this is the entire page: ```tsx import * as React from 'react'; import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'; import { Popover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'; function App() { return ( Open

No focusable content here.

 ); } createRoot(document.getElementById('root')).render(); ``` Steps to reproduce: 1. Render the component above as the only content of the page (`document.body` must not contain any other button, link, input, or other tabbable node — only the trigger and, once opened, the popup). 2. The popup opens (`defaultOpen`) and, because it has no focusable descendants, Base UI gives its container `tabindex="-1"` and moves initial focus onto it automatically. 3. Press Tab once. 4. The page throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` instead of closing the popup and moving focus on. Observed on the page above, served by Vite 8.2 in development, React 19.2.4, Chrome (headless, driven by Playwright). Before the keypress the only tabbable nodes in the document are the trigger button and Base UI's own focus guards (`[data-base-ui-focus-guard]`), and `document.activeElement` is the popup container (`div[role="dialog"]`, `tabindex="-1"`). A single `Tab` produces: ``` RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. at handleFocusTargetFocus (@base-ui_react_popover.js:6559:120) at executeDispatch (react-dom_client.js:9139:5) at runWithFiberInDEV (react-dom_client.js:850:66) at processDispatchQueue (react-dom_client.js:9165:27) at react-dom_client.js:9452:5 at batchedUpdates$1 (react-dom_client.js:2039:37) at dispatchEventForPluginEventSystem (react-dom_client.js:9238:4) at dispatchEvent (react-dom_client.js:11317:29) at dispatchDiscreteEvent (react-dom_client.js:11299:56) at handlePreFocusGuardFocus (@base-ui_react_popover.js:6555:55) ``` — the two guard handlers calling each other, as described above. The error is raised nine times in a row as React re-runs the handler; afterwards the popup is closed (`[data-open]` and `role="dialog"` are gone from the DOM) and `document.activeElement` has fallen back to `document.body`. The same crash is expected with `Menu` in place of `Popover`, since `Menu.Trigger` shares `useTriggerFocusGuards` with `Popover.Trigger`; that variant was not run. ## Base UI version 1.7.0 ## Which browser are you using? Chrome ## Which OS are you using? macOS ## Which assistive tech are you using (if applicable)? None ## Additional context The crash was first hit in an application (Vite 8.2, React 19.2.4, Chrome) rather than in the snippet above; the snippet is a reduction of that case, arrived at by following the code path described in *Current behavior*, and then confirmed by running it. Related but not a duplicate: #5538 ("[Popover] openOnHover does not open on keyboard focus and causes reopening after dismissal", closed as incomplete) also reports `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` thrown from `FloatingFocusManager`, but under a different, unsupported usage pattern (manually calling `setOpen(true)` from the trigger's `onFocus` while `openOnHover` is set), with a focusable link inside the popup. That is a different code path from the one described here — this report's popup has no focusable content at all, and no custom `onFocus` handling is involved, only default `Tab` navigation.

# Bug report

## Current behavior

- Go to https://base-ui.com/react/components/select
- Select "Gala"
- Press the down arrow
- The select opens back up

## Expected behavior

The next item in the list should be selected. Compare with the default `<select>` element at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/select : after choosing an option, you can press up/down arrow to scroll through the options.

The original HTML behavior (tested in Firefox and Chrome on Windows) should be kept, as it makes it easier to scroll through all options (the common pattern is when a website suggests different themes in a dropdown, which makes it easy to view all the different themes).

## Base UI version

1.7.0 (latest in docs)

## Which browser are you using?

Firefox

## Which OS are you using?

Windows

comments.body:
Context from the shadcn report of the same issue ([shadcn-ui/ui#11757](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui/issues/11757)): we dug into the implementation, and this is not a straightforward bug - the current behavior is actually the WAI-ARIA APG combobox pattern working as specified.

**Why the popup opens**

The Select trigger renders with `role="combobox"` + `aria-haspopup="listbox"`. Per the APG combobox pattern, ArrowDown on a closed combobox is supposed to open the popup and move focus to the first option. `useListNavigation` implements exactly that: with the popup closed, an arrow key calls `openOnNavigationKeyDown()` (default `openOnArrowKeyDown: true`), so the popup opens instead of changing the value.

The native `<select>` is a different pattern (a listbox, not a combobox), which is why it changes the selection without opening.

**The inconsistency**

Here's the interesting part: Select already commits values with the popup closed via typeahead. If the trigger is focused and you type "a", the value changes to the first matching option without the popup ever opening (tests: "commits typeahead on a closed trigger"). So closed-trigger value changes already exist for letters - just not for arrows.

**A possible direction**

An opt-in prop on Select.Root (something like `keyboardNavigation="native"` or `arrowKeysChangeValue`) that makes ArrowUp/ArrowDown commit the next/previous value while the popup is closed would match the native `<select>` behavior for the theme-switcher use case without breaking the APG default. The typeahead closed-trigger path proves the plumbing exists (values are registered in a ref while closed, and `setValue` is called directly).

The same pattern is being discussed for Radix ([radix-ui/themes#804](https://github.com/radix-ui/themes/issues/804)), so a maintainer opinion on the intended model here would settle it for the ecosystem.

Hi @Zezombye, Base UI's Select follows the macOS native `<select>` behavior, where `ArrowDown` on a focused closed select opens the menu rather than changing the value (and more relevantly, the APG select-only combobox pattern which specifies the same thing for use across all platforms). Typeahead committing a value while closed also matches macOS. 

The Windows convention of cycling values with arrows is a platform difference with the native select element. The element follows macOS and not Windows because of the APG guide.

> as it makes it easier to scroll through all options (the common pattern is when a website suggests different themes in a dropdown, which makes it easy to view all the different themes).

You can't rely on this UX affordance because macOS (as stated above) does it differently to begin with. So for all users to get the same experience, an alternative needs to be used, e.g. changing (temporarily) on pointer move/focus of each option rather than a selection. This hover technique, for example, is what Photoshop does with its blend mode select picker
